name: Technique - Wavetable scan and sub
description: Standalone technique from the Ableton Wavetable checklist: two tables, Env 2 scanning, mono sub, retriggered filter LFO and drive.

manual.instruction: Load two gnarly wavetables and blend them; lower the second oscillator's level. Use Envelope 2 with an up-then-down shape on both oscillator positions.
manual.verify: Both tables scan together and the patch has a deliberate vowel-like movement.
manual.why: Push Patterns layers Sapphire and Ruby and assigns Envelope 2 to both oscillator positions.

manual.instruction: Switch Wavetable to Mono and enable the sub oscillator. Set the filter LFO to retrigger with a 1/16 rate and a slower attack.
manual.verify: The bass is centered, has a clean sub, and the filter breathes in time.
manual.why: Push Patterns uses mono, the sub oscillator and a retriggered 1/16 filter LFO.

manual.instruction: Drive the oscillator into the filter, then add a short, low reverb send. Keep the sub and transient tight.
manual.verify: The growl is aggressive but not washed out.
manual.why: Push Patterns drives Wavetable into the filter and uses a restrained reverb.

manual.instruction: Try a custom table from a recorded vowel or one-shot and rescan it with the same modulation.
manual.verify: The patch becomes unique rather than a stock table.
manual.why: Push Patterns loads a user sample as a custom wavetable.

notes: Source: Push Patterns, 'How To Make DUBSTEP BASS Sounds with WAVETABLE In Ableton Live' (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nbmxDxKji9M). Transcript summary, not quotes. Reference-only because the engine cannot create or verify Wavetable patches.
